final.title: Spot free-tier limits before they break a workflow
final.body:
If you are a small-business owner who has tried ChatGPT but has not wired AI into a real workflow yet, this is a useful bounded decision: do you know when a free-tier tool is about to stop being free?

That includes SaaS plans, API usage, email tools, or any service that quietly turns a convenience into a bill or a block. The question is not whether the tool can do the job. It is whether you know the quota and check usage before the limit is hit.

A simple next step is to pick one tool in your stack and write down three things: the free limit, where usage is visible, and what alert or reminder will make you look at it. For some tools, a weekly calendar check is enough. For faster-moving usage, a vendor cost-alert email is better. Keep it boring. Boring is useful here.

Why this matters: hitting a free-tier limit unexpectedly can interrupt a workflow or force an unplanned upgrade while you are still deciding whether the process is worth automating. Early spotting does not make that decision for you, but it keeps it human and deliberate.

So the practical move is plain: list the quota limits in your current stack, then choose one to monitor first.
